steps.decide: What is accepted: types, sizes, counts, and which of those the server also enforces
How each file reports queued, uploading, done, failed and cancelled, independently
How retry works without re-sending what already succeeded
What cancel means: stop the transfer, keep the partial or discard it
Whether dropping is the only route, and how paste and keyboard upload work

rules.statement: Accepted types, maximum size and maximum count are stated before the drop and enforced again on the server, because the client check is a courtesy and the server check is the rule.
Each file owns its own state and progress; one failing file never marks the batch failed, and the batch summary counts done, failed and remaining out loud.
Retry resumes from the last confirmed chunk or restarts that file only; a retry that re-sends the whole batch is a data-loss risk on a metered connection.
Cancel stops the transfer, removes the partial where the server supports it, and says so; cancelling mid-upload never leaves an orphan file nobody can see.
The dropzone is a real button with a file input behind it, paste works for images where the context implies it, and dragging is never the only path.
Every queued file shows its name (mid-truncated), size and type, because two files called screenshot.png are the normal case, not the edge case.

stateMachine.staleResponseRule: progress and results are keyed by file id and upload attempt; a progress event from a cancelled or superseded attempt is discarded

transitions.trigger: files are dragged over the dropzone

motion.motion: the border brightens over 120ms and the hint changes
motion.reducedMotion: the border brightens instantly with no movement

transitions.trigger: the drop is accepted and the transfer starts

motion.motion: each row appears with its own progress bar over 120ms
motion.reducedMotion: rows appear instantly with a text percentage

motion.motion: the row's bar fills and turns to the done state over 160ms
motion.reducedMotion: the row jumps to done instantly and is announced once

motion.motion: that row gains an error line and a retry over 120ms while other rows continue
motion.reducedMotion: the row gains the error instantly

transitions.trigger: retry is pressed for one file

motion.motion: the row returns to its pending state over 120ms
motion.reducedMotion: the row returns to pending instantly

motion.motion: the row stops and states what was discarded over 120ms
motion.reducedMotion: the row stops instantly and the statement appears

motion.motion: the focus ring disappears with no delay
motion.reducedMotion: identical — the ring is immediate in both cases

motion.noneReason: unavailability is a permission or load fact, not an animation; the control states why instead of moving

sections.intent: Get files from the reader's device to the server with an honest per-file account of what is queued, moving, done, failed or cancelled.
useCases: attach three invoices to a record
retry a failed 40 MB upload without starting over
nicheDifferences: Uploads are the state machine most products get wrong, because they are the only common flow with N parallel async objects
The reader needs per-file truth, not a batch spinner
inputs: accepted types, size limits and count limits, and where they are enforced
whether the server supports resumable chunks and deletion of partials
the largest realistic file and the slowest realistic connection
anatomy: a dropzone that is also a button
a queue where each row owns state, name, size and progress
styling: rows are 56 px, name mid-truncated, size right-aligned in tabular numerals
progress is a 4 px bar under the name plus a text percentage
failed rows use the danger colour plus an icon and text
a11y: the dropzone is a button with a visible label; drag is an enhancement
each row's state is text as well as colour
progress announces at most about once a second per file
retry and cancel are buttons with the file name in their accessible name
responsive: at 320 px each row becomes two lines: name, then state and size
the queue never becomes a horizontally scrolled table
the dropzone stays 44 px tall and full-width on touch
copy: an empty queue reads 'Drop files here, or choose from your device — PDF, PNG up to 20 MB'
a failure reads 'Invoice-2026-03.pdf failed: 28 MB is over the 20 MB limit'
a cancel reads 'Cancelled after 4.1 MB; the partial file was removed'
alternatives: a camera capture when the file is a photo taken now
a link-based import for files already in cloud storage
a background job with email notification for very large sets
acceptance: constraints are stated before the drop and enforced on the server
each file reports queued, uploading, done, failed or cancelled independently
retry resumes the failed file only and never re-sends completed files
cancel states exactly what happened to the partial
the dropzone is operable by keyboard and paste works where meaningful
failureCases: one failed file marks the whole batch failed and hides the nine that succeeded
retry restarts every file, wasting the completed ones
cancel leaves a partial upload on the server with no record
drag is the only path and a keyboard user cannot upload at all

refused.reason: an unavailable uploader explains why in place rather than rendering a dead dropzone
a compact attach button has no drop target; it opens the picker instead
